newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco sets up national body to monitor elections.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sets up national body to monitor elections.

text.p: Morocco created a national commission on Monday to supervise local and legislative elections due in June, the official MAP news agency said.
"A national commission in charge of following up all electoral operations this year was set up," MAP said. The body was created by Moroccan King Hassan II, it added.

According to a royal decree (Dahir Royal), the commission is chaired by supreme court president Driss Dahak and includes interior, justice ministers and members of political parties represented in the existing parliament, MAP said.
Morocco has 10 political parties represented in the 333-seat Chamber of Representatives (parliament), including four opposition groups with a total 125 seats.
More than 13 million voters, or nearly half Morocco's population, will be called on June 13, 1997 to elect members of nearly 1,600 communal and municipal councils, the interior ministry said.
Around 25,000 councillors will be elected during the same period, it added.
The councils will later elect representatives in a new Upper House of parliament being set up under constitutional reforms approved last September.
Voting will be held throughout the country, including the disputed Western Sahara territory.

The local elections are the first of a series which will culminate in parliamentary elections in September, with a new bicameral parliament being inaugurated by King Hassan on the second Friday of October.
Under the new constitution, the Lower House of parliament will be directly elected through universal suffrage.
The Upper House will have power to vote a no-confidence motion in the government and could legally overthrow it.
